messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: P1 — routing tail latency spike detected in region us-west-2. p99 increased from ~180ms to ~3s over the last 5m, streaming stall alerts from multiple clients. Triggered by routing-health-alerts. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.net/alerts/1738502460

oncall-sre: Ack — I'm oncall and looking. Collecting router logs and recently-applied rollout history. Initial hypothesis: recent load-splitting rollout to 'loadsplit-v2' in usw2. Will post findings.

alex: I can take runtime diagnostics. From infra metrics: misroute_count spiked ~x10, tail_kv_cache_miss increased. Quick snippet from edge-router logs (last 5m):
```
[router][usw2] misroute_count=423 tail_p99=3120ms streaming_stalls=78 policy=loadsplit-v2
[router][usw2] weight_update: policy=loadsplit-v2 target=0.6 -> 0.72 src=policy-controller
```
Looks like weight oscillation leading to hot partitioning.

maya: We rolled out loadsplit-v2 ~14m ago as a follow-up to the sharding change. Canary looked fine in euw1 but usw2 traffic profile is burstier, exposing a heuristic bug in the split logic. Reverting the policy now.

cheng: Revert command ready if ops want manual flip. Temporary mitigation: force traffic to legacy policy (loadsplit-v1) in usw2 and disable the auto-rollout controller for that region. Commands: 
```bash
# force stable policy in us-west-2
redwoodctl routing set-policy --region=us-west-2 --policy=loadsplit-v1 --force
# pause controller
redwoodctl rollout pause --controller=policy-controller --region=us-west-2
```
I'm standing by to run.

oncall-sre: Do it. Executed at 1738503100. Setting manual weight to 1.0 for loadsplit-v1 in usw2. Will monitor p95/p99 and streaming metrics.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Command acknowledged: redwoodctl routing set-policy --region=us-west-2 --policy=loadsplit-v1 --force (executed by cheng at 2024-06-08T18:05:00Z).

lisa: Support note — we've received three Priority customer reports (acct: fin-apis, chatflow, docsearch) with repeated streaming disconnects and >2s generation latencies. Raising potential SLA exposures. I'm aggregating logs; will send a customer-facing status.

ryan: Observability update: after the manual flip at 1738503100 metrics trending back down. p99 dropped from 3s -> 210ms over 6 minutes. Streaming stall alerts count decreasing. Patch appears effective.

alex: Good. Root cause looks like a policy heuristic that mis-evaluated key entropy for sessions with high prefix-sharing; it favored splitting keys into a new shard, concentrating hot keys on a small subset of backends. Proposed short-term fix: revert rollout + pin hotkey-aware routing. Long-term: adjust loadsplit scoring, add synthetic canary with bursty prefix distribution.

maya: Agreed. I've opened an ENG ticket: ENG-rt-1792 "loadsplit: stabilize scoring for bursty prefix distributions" and added owners: alex, cheng. Also scheduling postmortem.

oncall-sre: Current status: mitigation applied, customer impact ongoing but improving. Open actions: 1) keep manual policy in place for 24h, 2) add telemetry for per-prefix entropy to detect early, 3) run evictions simulation for loadsplit-v2.

lisa: Posted interim customer status: "We are mitigating a network routing issue impacting latency for some customers in us-west-2. We have applied a rollback and are monitoring; next update in 30 minutes."

cheng: For the postmortem we'll capture these artifacts: rollout diff, router logs, policy-controller events and an artifact of the canary test. Quick diff that likely caused it: 
```diff
- split_threshold: 0.9
+ split_threshold: 0.75  # more aggressive splitting; lowered entropy bar caused fragmentation in usw2
```

oncall-sre: Handing off to day SRE at 1738503600. I am moving to monitoring-only. If any regression occurs ping @oncall-sre.

ryan: Final note — traffic stabilized. p95 back to ~50ms, p99 ~200ms, streaming stalls negligible. Scheduling a live postmortem with eng-runtime + eng-platform + eng-sre. Tentative time: 2024-06-09T15:00:00Z.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) by oncall-sre at 1738503720. Severity: P1 -> mitigated, next step: postmortem. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
